1873: The Rothschilds, the First Great Depression, and the Making of the Modern World — Liaquat Ahamed (Non-fiction)
Why Fred: 2026 FT Business Book of the Year shortlist, from the Pulitzer-winning author of Lords of Finance. It tells the railway boom and the bust that followed, the same Panic-of-1873 capital cycle his Djukanovic page applies to AI capex. Kirkus gave it a star; History Today doubts the "great depression" framing.

We Shall Outlast Them: Putin's Global Campaign to Defeat the West — Hanna Notte (Non-fiction)
Why Fred: A Russia analyst argues the Kremlin is fighting over global order, not only Ukraine, with on-the-ground detail such as sanctions evasion. It follows Red Notice and Chokepoints and fits his Dalio alliance-bloc and G-Zero pages.

Morbid: Debunking Modern Longevity Science — Saul Justin Newman (Non-fiction)
Why Fred: An Oxford demographer (2024 Ig Nobel) shows the Blue Zones and centenarian records rest on bad data, and follows the money in anti-ageing products. It's a sceptic's check on his health/longevity reading after Breath and the Outlive suggestion.

Taiwan Travelogue — Yáng Shuāng-zǐ, tr. Lin King (Literary Fiction)
Why Fred: Outside territory. 2026 International Booker winner. A Japanese novelist tours colonial Taiwan in 1938 with her Taiwanese interpreter; a love story between two women told through food writing, footnotes and a fake-translation frame.

The Most Dangerous Trade: How Short Sellers Uncover Fraud, Keep Markets Honest, and Make and Lose Billions — Richard Teitelbaum (Non-fiction)
Why Fred: Profiles a dozen-plus famous short sellers (Chanos, Einhorn, Ackman and others): how they find targets, fund the position and survive the squeeze. It's the practitioner side of his short-research pages and his live ORCL short.

Off the Scales: The Inside Story of Ozempic and the Race to Cure Obesity — Aimee Donnellan (Non-fiction)
Why Fred: 2026 FT Business Book of the Year shortlist. Traces GLP-1 from early lab work to Novo Nordisk's rise and its fight with Lilly. It covers both his health/longevity interest and his Novo Nordisk research page.

The Infinity Machine: Demis Hassabis, DeepMind and the Quest for Superintelligence — Sebastian Mallaby (Non-fiction)
Why Fred: 2026 FT shortlist from a past winner (More Money Than God), based on 30+ hours with Hassabis. It's the human story behind his AI & Tech foundation-model pages.

John of John — Douglas Stuart (Literary Fiction)
Why Fred: Outside territory. A 2026 Booker shortlist novel from the Shuggie Bain winner. A young art graduate comes home to his strict Free Presbyterian father's croft on Harris; a quiet father-son family drama.
